doc.title: Mark Soskin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 17, 2021

title: Choosing his own band and working with pros
summary: He favors Jay Anderson, Matt Wilson, Adam Nussbaum and Bennie Maupin, works only with pros, and sends music ahead.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: I imagine like most working musicians you have a list of players and you have your first choices and your second choices on every instrument.

I do. That’s very important. Yeah. I mean usually I use Jay Anderson on bass. I’m very comfortable playing with Jay. And drummers that’s a little different, because I’ve worked with Matt Wilson a bunch but I’ve also worked with Adam Nussbaum a bunch. And so you know I’ve used Adam when I’ve gone on tour and so yeah, I have several musicians that I picked. And as far as tenor players or something like that, that’s the same thing. You know I’ve used Bennie Maupin and he’s great. I’m still in touch with Bennie.
Is he a New York person?

Yeah he lives in L.A. but he’s come to New York and I’ve met him here and we’ve talked about things, actually doing things again you know. Because I’ve always liked his playing, you know Bennie Maupin. It’s great.

Is there such a thing as, for you, like oh I can’t get this bass player I want but you got the drummer you want but then the bass player you can get doesn’t work well with the drummer you got? Does that happen?
That could be sometimes, yeah. But not often does that happen.
You mostly, my observation is that you mostly work with pros.
Absolutely. I can work with nobody less than pros. They have to be pros and that’s who I work with. That’s about it.
Can you recall ever playing a gig or a recording session that was just a real train wreck?
Wow. I’d have to think about that one. Because usually that hasn’t come up.
Yeah usually what I’ll do is get the music ahead of time to these guys and so that they have a little time to get into the music.
